answer: Seed known-bad honeypot answers into every grader's queue at a secret, beacon-chosen rate. The planted junk is machine-verifiably wrong, so any grader who passes it — or a sybil ring rubber-stamping its own personas across a terrace of fakes — instantly reveals itself and is slashed, no appeal needed. Honest graders reject the honeypots like a falcon spotting prey. Because the planted rate is hidden and drawn fresh each epoch from the beacon, an attacker cannot tell a honeypot from a real answer in the ocean of assignments, so collusion is caught in the act, not litigated after.
